scope: Windows v0.1 platform, network, and continuous-integration boundary. No cloud runtime, production deployment, signing, updater, or production credentials are introduced.

implementation.businessRuleBoundary: The workflow compiles and exercises the shared download-engine crate consumed by the Tauri shell. It adds no transfer, lifecycle, persistence, filename, collision, progress, or clipboard business rules.
implementation.release: CI evidence only; no packaging publication, deployment, signing, or updater

networkBoundary.model: Local-first desktop client making user-initiated outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests through reqwest in the shared engine.
networkBoundary.runtimeEvidenceOwner: packages/download-engine/tests/runtime.rs provides controlled loopback HTTP Range and Range-ignored behavior; ENG-15 owns independent disposition.

controls: job timeout prevents an unbounded runner
concurrency cancellation avoids redundant work for the same ref
engine tests and desktop compilation use crate lockfiles

traceability.limitation: Independent verification remains reserved for ENG-15.

verificationNotes: The CI workflow is inspectable and executes on a real Windows runner when triggered.
Local verification is recorded by the WS-08 engineering-workstream result and is not an independent disposition.
No user-visible behavior was changed in this platform workstream, so DOM or desktop-runtime behavioral evidence is not applicable here.
knownRisks: The write boundary excludes root Cargo.toml and LICENSE, so CI cannot use a root workspace command and this workstream cannot add the required root GPL-3.0 text.
windows-latest is a moving runner image; release builds should later pin and document a supported Windows and toolchain matrix.
The workflow action is version-tag pinned rather than commit-digest pinned; repository policy may require a stronger supply-chain pin before release.
CI checks compilation but does not sign, package, install, upgrade, rollback, or uninstall an artifact.
Proxy, trust-store, firewall, endpoint-security, and real network-interruption behavior still require Windows runtime verification.
Only ENG-15 may issue independent engineering verification.
